To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) sprout formation is accelerated in axons that are proximal to the site of a conditioning lesion; (2) sprout formation occurs in axons that have undergone a conditioning lesion, even when the axon has not been transected; and (3) sprout formation in axons that undergo a conditioning lesion is not associated with the presence of degenerating myelin.
a conditioning lesion of a nerve trunk induces earlier sprout formation than does a lesion alone, and that the conditioning lesion does not induce axonal death.
a conditioning lesion accelerates sprout formation in the rat sciatic and sciatic–femoral nerves.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the axolemma in axonal sprout development.
the role of the conditioning lesion in axonal regeneration and the formation of axonal sprouts at nodes of Ranvier.
the effect of a conditioning injury on the time course of axonal sprouting in myelinated fibers of the peripheral nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a conditioning lesion accelerates the time‐course and incidence of type B axonal sprout development at nodes of Ranvier.
the conditioning lesion induced a significant increase in sprout formation at the nodes of Ranvier.
the conditioning lesion accelerates sprout formation by 18 hours, but the effect is not maintained beyond 27 hours.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a conditioning lesion increases sprout formation at the nodes of Ranvier in myelinated fibers of rat sciatic nerve.
the conditioning lesion induces sprout formation, which is followed by the development of a cytoskeleton and a subsequent period of sprout degeneration.
the conditioning lesion induces sprout formation at the nodes of Ranvier and that this sprout formation precedes sprout formation at other axonal sites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conditioning lesion induced an earlier onset of axonal sprouts at nodes of Ranvier.
the conditioning lesion induced a change in the time‐course for the formation of sprouts that is not attributable to the presence of a putative factor from pre‐degeneration axons.

the axonal response to a conditioning lesion is not a simple increase in sprouting, but a complex response in which sprouting may be accompanied by retraction, myelin degenerations, axonal degenerations and/or sprout degeneration.
